subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should OpenClaw preserve first-entry default routing as the core contract, or require/warn/migrate when `agents.list` first displaces the implicit `main` agent?
rationale: The behavior is source-reproducible and security-sensitive, but every suggested fix changes config/default routing semantics for existing users.

options.title: Warn and doctor-repair implicit-main displacement
options.body: Keep first-entry fallback for compatibility, but add config/doctor/operator warnings and a guided fix when `agents.list` has no explicit default and existing `main` state is present.

options.title: Require explicit defaults
options.body: Make non-empty `agents.list` without one `default: true` invalid or fail-closed, which is clearer but may break existing configs on upgrade.

options.title: Keep current behavior documented only
options.body: Treat first-entry fallback as intentional and document the explicit `main` workaround without code changes, accepting the current foot-gun.

recommendation.title: Warn and doctor-repair implicit-main displacement
recommendation.body: Keep first-entry fallback for compatibility, but add config/doctor/operator warnings and a guided fix when `agents.list` has no explicit default and existing `main` state is present.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame on the default-routing files points to this owner candidate, and the decision is a compatibility-sensitive core routing policy choice.
